query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small, controlled amount of titanium into boride-based components will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard boride-based components as used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment without titanium modification.
generation.intervention: Doping the boride matrix with a low percentage of titanium during processing (or via a surface modification step) to modify interfacial chemistry.
generation.conditions: Exposure to high-temperature molten aluminum typical of hot-dip plating processes, under standard operational exposure times and thermal conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Ti-enriched interfacial layer or modified boride microstructure that resists aluminum penetration.
generation.mechanism: Titanium is expected to segregate to grain boundaries or surfaces during processing, leading to the formation of a thin, stable, titanium-containing phase (or interfacial layer) that inhibits aluminum diffusion and direct chemical reaction with the boride phase. This protective layer reduces the corrosion kinetics compared to undoped boride.
generation.predicted_outcome: Titanium-doped boride components will exhibit a lower corrosion rate under molten-aluminum exposure (e.g., a measurable reduction in weight loss or pit formation compared to untreated boride components).
generation.baseline: The performance of conventional boride components without titanium doping under identical hot-dip aluminum conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected as long as the titanium content is kept low enough to preserve the integrity of the boride phase and prevent formation of any deleterious secondary phases that might compromise mechanical properties.
generation.uncertainty: The exact optimal titanium concentration and the degree of corrosion resistance improvement are uncertain and need to be determined through systematic experimental optimization.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of boride-based components: one with a controlled amount of titanium doping and a control set without titanium. Subject both sets to a standardized hot-dip aluminum plating process where they are immersed in molten aluminum under identical temperature and time conditions. After exposure, compare the corrosion behavior of both sets.
measurements: Weight loss measurements to quantify material removal due to corrosion
Surface and cross-sectional microstructural analysis (using SEM/EDS) to identify the presence and continuity of any Ti-enriched protective layer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the titanium-doped components do not show a statistically significant improvement (for example, at least a 10% reduction in weight loss and evidence of a protective Ti-containing interfacial phase) compared to the control, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Effect of Ti on Characterization and Properties of CoCrFeNiTix High Entropy Alloy Prepared Via Electro-Deoxidization of the Metal Oxides and Vacuum Hot Pressing Sintering Process

Abstract: The CoCrFeNi system is one of the most important high entropy alloys (HEAs) systems. By adding and adjusting the alloy element components and using different synthesis methods, different phases, organization and microstructure can be obtained, thus improving their properties. In this study, CoCrFeNiTix HEAs with various Ti contents (x in molar ratio, x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) were fabricated by an electrochemical process by virtue of different oxides. The impacts of different Ti contents on the structure, distribution of elements, mechanical properties and corrosion behavior were researched using XRD, EDX and other testing methods. The bulk CoCrFeNiTix (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) HEAs could be obtained through vacuum hot pressing sintering process (VHPS), which had a single-phase FCC structure. The results of the study showed that the bulk CoCrFeNiTix exhibited superior ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and hardness, with the UTS of CoCrFeNiTi as high as 783 MPa and the hardness of CoCrFeNiTi1.5 reaching 6
